mainTopic: Penalties that pass to heirs, and permitted work, buying and moving on חול המועד
overview: The amud opens by asking whether a man who planned his work for חול המועד and then died passes his penalty on to his son. רבי זירא proves from a משנה about a field improved during שביעית that such a penalty is on the person, not the money, so the son is not penalized. אביי adds a similar tradition about someone who made another person's טהרות impure. Next comes a משנה limiting purchases on חול המועד, with an exception for a seller who has nothing to eat. רבא and רב נחמן discuss whether a hungry worker may also be hired for wages, and אביי proves from the משנה about loan documents that he may. רב ששת challenges this from the crafts allowed on ערב פסח. רב פפא and רבינא push back on his reasoning, and רב אשי explains that חול המועד and ערב פסח limit work for different reasons. A final משנה deals with moving belongings and bringing utensils from a craftsman. The גמרא resolves a contradiction about the utensils in two different ways.

steps.title: The firstborn case may not be a fair comparison
steps.stepSummary: With a בכור, the son is penalized after his father. But that may be because the sin there is a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slit the ear of a firstborn animal, the רבנן penalized his son after him. But that is because it is a Torah prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: This is part of the setup for the question. The גמרא brings a case where the son is penalized and explains why it may not apply to חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a blemish on a בכור goes against a Torah law, so the רבנן were extra strict and penalized the son too. Working on חול המועד is a lighter matter. So the בכור case does not prove that the son is penalized here.

keyTerms.meaning: a prohibition from the Torah itself

phrases.english: One who slit the ear of a firstborn animal
they penalized his son after him
that is because it is a Torah prohibition

steps.triggerLanguage: צָרַם אֹזֶן בְּכוֹר קָנְסוּ בְּנוֹ אַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by pushing aside a possible precedent for the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the son is penalized for his father's planned work on חול המועד.

steps.title: The slave-sold-to-a-non-Jew case may not be a fair comparison either
steps.stepSummary: With a slave sold to a non-Jew, the son is penalized too. But that is because every day the slave is kept from doing מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even if you will say that when someone sold his slave to a non-Jew and then died, the רבנן penalized his son after him, that is because every single day the slave is kept away from מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case where the son is penalized. It explains why this case is also different from חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the slave case, the harm keeps going: each day the slave is still kept from מצוות. So the penalty has to continue with the son. On חול המועד, the wrong act is already over and done.

keyTerms.meaning: and even if you will say

phrases.english: And even if you will say
one who sold his slave to a non-Jew and died
they penalized his son after him
that is because every day
he is taken away from מצוות
phrases.notes: He means the slave: while the non-Jew owns him, he can't keep the מצוות a slave is obligated in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר מָכַר עַבְדּוֹ לְגוֹי וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second precedent and shows why it is also different.

steps.title: The real question: was the person penalized, or the money?
steps.stepSummary: Here, what is the law? If the רבנן penalized the man, he is gone. If they penalized the money, it is still here.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law here? Did the רבנן penalize the man, and he is no longer alive? Or perhaps they penalized the money, and the money is still here!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the main question clearly. The answer depends on what the penalty was aimed at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the penalty was aimed at the person who sinned, it ends when he dies. If it was aimed at the money he earned through the forbidden work, it stays with the money even after it passes to his son.

keyTerms.meaning: he is not here / it is here

steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a penalty on the person and a penalty on the money comes up in many places in the גמרא.

phrases.english: What is the law here?
phrases.notes: Here means the man who planned his work for חול המועד and then died.

phrases.english: Did the רבנן penalize the man
and he is no longer here
or perhaps
the רבנן penalized the money
and it is still here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the precedents are pushed aside, the question is asked in its basic form.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רבנן's penalty aimed at the person, so it ends with his death, or at the money, so it passes to the heir?

steps.title: Proof from a field improved during שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers from a משנה about שביעית. רבי יוסי בר חנינא adds a tradition: if the owner improved the field and died, his son may sow it. So the penalty was only on the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this. A field that was cleared of thorns during שביעית may be sown after שביעית. If it was fertilized, or animals were penned on it to fertilize it, it may not be sown after שביעית. And רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: We have a tradition that if he improved it and died, his son may sow it. This shows the רבנן penalized him, but did not penalize his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question with a case already taught: a field improved in a forbidden way during שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Improving a field during שביעית is forbidden, so the רבנן banned sowing it afterward. But if the owner dies, his son may sow it. This shows that kind of penalty is aimed at the person, not the property.

keyTerms.meaning: the seventh year, when the land rests

phrases.english: He said to him: You have already learned it:
a field that was cleared of thorns during שביעית
may be sown in the year after שביעית
if it was fertilized, or animals were penned on it
it may not be sown in the year after שביעית

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: נָקְטִינַן,
phrases.english: And רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: We have a tradition
if he improved it and died
his son may sow it
This shows: the רבנן penalized him
but the רבנן did not penalize his son

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 3 using a case that was already taught.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rabbinic penalty for forbidden work is aimed at the wrongdoer himself, not at his heir.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית together with the tradition of רבי יוסי בר חנינא.

steps.title: So the son is not penalized for חול המועד work
steps.stepSummary: Applying the שביעית case: for work on חול המועד, too, only the father was penalized, not his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: the רבנן penalized him, but the רבנן did not penalize his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the שביעית rule to our question and gives the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the field, the penalty for planning work on חול המועד was aimed at the person. Once he dies, his son may benefit from the work.
steps.whatToRemember: A penalty the רבנן place on someone who did forbidden work is aimed at him personally. After he dies, his son is not penalized, just like with the field improved during שביעית.

phrases.english: Here too: the רבנן penalized him
but the רבנן did not penalize his son

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule proven in step 4 and applies it to חול המועד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The son of a man who planned his work for חול המועד is not penalized after his father dies.

steps.title: Making someone's pure food impure: the son is not penalized
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: if someone made another person's טהרות impure and then died, the son does not have to pay. The damage is not real damage by Torah law, so only the father was fined by the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition that if a person made someone else's pure food impure and then died, the רבנן did not penalize his son after him. Why? Damage you cannot see is not counted as damage. The רבנן fined the father himself, but they did not fine his son.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another case that matches what we just concluded about חול המועד: a rabbinic fine stays with the person and does not pass to his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making food טמא does not change how it looks, so by Torah law it is not damage. The only reason the person pays is a fine from the רבנן. That fine was placed on the person, not on his money, so his son is free. This is the same side of step 3's question (fine on the man, not on the money).

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition
He made someone else's pure food ritually impure
A penalty or fine set by the רבנן

steps.whatToRemember: When the רבנן fine a person for damage that is not real damage by Torah law, the fine is on him and not on his heirs.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
If he made [another's] pure items impure and died —
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets fills in what the גמרא assumes: it means someone else's pure food that this man ruined.

phrases.english: they did not penalize his son after him.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: הֶיזֵּק שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר לָא שְׁמֵיהּ הֶיזֵּק.
phrases.english: Damage that cannot be seen is not called damage.
The Rabbis penalized him himself,
they did not penalize his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel case that supports the conclusion in step 5: a rabbinic fine stays with the person and does not pass to the son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If someone made another's טהרות impure and died, his son does not pay, because the fine was only on the father.

steps.title: New משנה: buying houses, slaves and animals on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says you may not buy houses, slaves or animals on חול המועד. There are two exceptions: it is needed for the festival, or the seller has nothing to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may not buy houses, slaves or animals on חול המועד, unless it is for the needs of the festival, or for the needs of the seller who has nothing to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It limits business deals on חול המועד and gives two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Big purchases count as business, and business is not allowed on חול המועד. They become allowed if the festival needs them, or if a poor seller needs the money to eat. The second exception is what the גמרא will discuss next.

keyTerms.meaning: For the needs of the festival

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין לוֹקְחִין בָּתִּים עֲבָדִים וּבְהֵמָה
phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not buy houses, slaves, and animals
unless it is for the needs of the festival,
or for the needs of the seller
who has nothing to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of penalties ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying houses, slaves and animals on חול המועד is forbidden, except for the festival's needs or a seller who has nothing to eat.

steps.title: רבא asks: may a hungry person work for wages?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about a worker who has nothing to eat. May he be hired for pay on חול המועד?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבא asked רב נחמן: What is the law about wages for someone who has nothing to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks whether the משנה's "nothing to eat" exception also covers a poor person who wants to earn wages by working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה clearly lets a poor person sell what he owns. רבא wants to know whether a poor person may also do work that is normally not allowed on חול המועד, so he can be paid and eat.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava asked Rav Nahman:

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Wages for one who has nothing to eat, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether a poor worker may be hired to work on חול המועד so that he can eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the משנה's "nothing to eat" exception reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the "nothing to eat" exception allow hiring a poor worker for wages on חול המועד?

steps.title: רב נחמן tries to prove it from the extra words in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the משנה already teaches this. The words "who has nothing to eat" seem extra, so they must come to include wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned it: "or for the needs of the seller who has nothing to eat." What does this come to add? Doesn't it come to add wages for work?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tries to answer רבא straight from the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "For the needs of the seller" already says enough. Adding "who has nothing to eat" looks like it is meant to teach something more. רב נחמן suggests the extra thing is the case of a poor worker earning wages.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include?

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹכֵר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל.
phrases.english: Or for the needs of the seller who has nothing to eat.
What does this come to include?
Is it not to include wages for work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question with a proof from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: A poor person may work for wages on חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra words "שאין לו מה יאכל" in our משנה.

steps.title: רבא: the words only explain, they do not add
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof. "Who has nothing to eat" is not adding a new case. It just explains what "the needs of the seller" means.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No, it is only explaining.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof from "extra words" only works if the words really are extra. רבא says they are not: "the needs of the seller" could be unclear, so the משנה spells out that it means he has nothing to eat. That leaves no hint about wages.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
it is explaining.
phrases.notes: He means: these words just tell us what "the needs of the seller" are. They do not add a new case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, פָּרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from our משנה, not the possibility that wages are allowed. אביי's source in step 11 brings a new proof, and step 12 settles the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words are not extra. They explain what "the needs of the seller" means.

steps.title: אביי brings a משנה about writing loan documents
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא from another משנה. Loan documents may not be written on חול המועד, but they may be written if the lender doesn't trust the borrower or if "he has nothing to eat." Those words seem to include the wages of the scribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: We may not write loan documents on חול המועד. But if he does not trust him, or if he has nothing to eat, he may write it. "He has nothing to eat" comes to include what? Doesn't it come to include wages for work!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's rejection by bringing a different משנה where the words "nothing to eat" really cannot just be explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the loan-document משנה, nobody is selling anything, so "nothing to eat" cannot be explaining "the needs of the seller." The only person who earns from writing a document is the scribe. So the words must mean a poor scribe may write it to earn his wages.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two "nothing to eat" people. In this משנה it is not the lender or the borrower; the גמרא reads it as the scribe who earns wages for writing.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
We may not write loan documents on the festival,
phrases.notes: This is a different משנה later in this מסכת, on 18b.

phrases.english: but if he does not trust him,
phrases.notes: The lender is worried he won't get paid back without a written document.

phrases.english: or if he has nothing to eat —
he may write it.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי?
phrases.english: "He has nothing to eat" — what does this come to include?
Is it not to include wages for work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rejection in step 10 by bringing a source where "nothing to eat" cannot be just an explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that "nothing to eat" only explains and does not include wages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the loan-document משנה there is no seller to explain, so "nothing to eat" must be adding the case of a poor scribe earning wages.

steps.title: Conclusion: a poor person may work for wages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts אביי's proof. A person who has nothing to eat may be hired to work for wages on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question: the proof from the loan-document משנה stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's push-back does not work against the second משנה. So the answer to רבא's question in step 8 is yes: work for wages is allowed for someone who has nothing to eat.
steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, someone who has nothing to eat may sell his things and may also work for wages, even doing work that is normally not allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the "nothing to eat" exception is broad. It covers earning money by working, not only selling things you own.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts אביי's proof from step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hiring a poor worker who has nothing to eat, for wages, is allowed on חול המועד.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes the three crafts allowed on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins a challenge by quoting a teaching. On ערב פסח, only tailors, barbers and launderers may work until midday, because similar work is allowed on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: The חכמים say three crafts may work on ערב פסח until midday: tailors, barbers and launderers. Tailors may work because an ordinary person may sew in his normal way on חול המועד. Barbers and launderers may work because people who come back from overseas, or someone who gets out of prison, may get a haircut and wash clothes on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is setting up a challenge against the ruling in step 12. Here he only quotes his source; the attack itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay attention to how the source reasons. Each craft is allowed on ערב פסח because some similar form of that work is allowed on חול המועד. רב ששת will use this exact pattern in his attack.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection, challenging from a source
An ordinary person, not a professional
The intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
And the Sages say,
three crafts may do work
on the eve of Pesach until midday:
the tailors, the barbers, and the launderers.
The tailors, because an ordinary person may sew in his usual way
on the intermediate days of the festival.

phrases.aramaic: הַסַּפָּרִין וְהַכּוֹבְסִין — שֶׁכֵּן הַבָּאִין מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם
phrases.english: The barbers and the launderers, because those who come from overseas
and one who leaves prison

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּרִין לְסַפֵּר וּלְכַבֵּס בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: are permitted to cut hair and wash clothes on the intermediate days of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the conclusion of step 12 by bringing in an outside source about ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a person who has nothing to eat may be hired for wages on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The source shows that whatever kind of work is allowed on חול המועד is also allowed on ערב פסח.

steps.title: If wage work were allowed, all work would be allowed on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת draws his conclusion. If hired work for a hungry person were allowed on חול המועד, then every kind of work should be allowed on ערב פסח, and it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that working for wages, for someone who has nothing to eat, is allowed on חול המועד, then all kinds of work should also be allowed on ערב פסח. After all, there is the case of wages for someone who has nothing to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his attack. If hungry workers may be hired on חול המועד, then by the source's own logic any work should be allowed on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wage work for a hungry person could involve any job at all. So if it is allowed on חול המועד, every craft would have a matching case on חול המועד, and every craft would be allowed on ערב פסח. But the source allows only three crafts. That suggests wage work must be forbidden on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind, meaning 'if you were to think'

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is not talking about the hungry worker on ערב פסח. He is using the ערב פסח list to prove what must be forbidden on חול המועד.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל שְׁרֵי —
phrases.english: that wages for one who has nothing to eat is permitted,
then all labors should also be permitted,
phrases.notes: He means permitted on ערב פסח morning, following the same pattern as the three crafts.

phrases.english: since there is the case of wages for work
for one who has nothing to eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source quoted in step 13 to attack the ruling of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 12 that a person who has nothing to eat may be hired for wages on חול המועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source allows work on ערב פסח when similar work is allowed on חול המועד. Hungry-worker wages cover every kind of work. So if they were allowed, all work would be allowed on ערב פסח, which contradicts the list of only three crafts.

steps.title: רב פפא: then building would be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא shows that רב ששת's logic proves too much. A leaning wall may be rebuilt on חול המועד, yet building is not allowed on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: If so, building should also be allowed on ערב פסח, since a wall leaning over the public street may be torn down and rebuilt in the normal way on חול המועד because of the danger!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back against רב ששת's method. He shows it would lead to an obviously wrong result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuilding a dangerous wall is allowed on חול המועד, but nobody says building in general is allowed on ערב פסח. So the ערב פסח list cannot mean that every special allowance on חול המועד carries over to ערב פסח. רב ששת's proof therefore falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, meaning 'if your logic were right'

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objects to this:
If so, building should be permitted,
since a wall leaning toward the public domain
one may tear down and rebuild in the usual way
because of the danger!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's reasoning from step 14 by showing it leads to an unacceptable result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The method of comparing ערב פסח to every special allowance on חול המועד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The method proves too much. By the same logic, building would be allowed on ערב פסח because of the leaning-wall case.

steps.title: רבינא: then a scribe would be allowed too
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds a second example. Some documents may be written on חול המועד, yet a scribe is not allowed to work on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: If so, a scribe should also be allowed to work on ערב פסח, since betrothal documents, divorce documents and receipts may be written on חול המועד!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives another example that shows רב ששת's logic proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some documents may be written on חול המועד, but scribes are not on the list of crafts allowed on ערב פסח. This confirms that the three crafts are a limited list, not a rule that copies every חול המועד allowance. So the ruling of step 12 still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת tried to prove that hiring a hungry worker is forbidden on חול המועד, using the ערב פסח list. רב פפא and רבינא challenged his logic, since it would also allow building and scribal work on ערב פסח. The גמרא then turns to a more basic answer from רב אשי (step 17).

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objects to this:
If so, a scribe should be permitted,
since one may write betrothal documents,
divorce documents, and receipts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection, parallel to רב פפא's in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The same method used by רב ששת in step 14.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much. By the same logic, scribes would be allowed to work on ערב פסח because some documents may be written on חול המועד.

steps.title: רב אשי: the two days limit work for different reasons
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers רב ששת's challenge in a new way. On חול המועד work is limited because it is a strain, so the רבנן allowed it to prevent a loss. On ערב פסח work is limited so people can prepare for יום טוב, so only work needed for יום טוב is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Are you comparing חול המועד to the fourteenth of ניסן? On חול המועד, work is limited because it is a strain, and where there is a loss the רבנן allowed it. On the fourteenth, work is limited for the sake of יום טוב's needs. So whatever is needed for יום טוב the רבנן allowed, and whatever is not needed for יום טוב they did not allow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a different approach from רב פפא and רבינא. He says רב ששת's comparison does not work in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת assumed that anything allowed on חול המועד should also be allowed on ערב פסח. רב אשי shows that the two days restrict work for different reasons. On חול המועד the issue is effort, so a loss (like a hungry person with no food) can override it. On ערב פסח the issue is getting ready for יום טוב, so only work that helps יום טוב is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Are you raising a contradiction / comparing?
What is needed for the Festival
The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח

steps.whatToRemember: חול המועד limits work because of strain, so a loss can permit it. ערב פסח limits work so people can prepare for יום טוב, so only work for יום טוב is permitted. That is why hiring out a hungry person on חול המועד says nothing about ערב פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the earlier conclusion that a person who has nothing to eat may work for wages on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Are you comparing the Festival days to the fourteenth?
phrases.notes: "The fourteenth" is the fourteenth of ניסן, which is ערב פסח.

phrases.english: The Festival days: the limit is because of strain,
and where there is a loss, the Rabbis permitted it.

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר — מִשּׁוּם צוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב הוּא.
phrases.english: The fourteenth: the limit is for the sake of the Festival's needs.

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּצוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב שָׁרוּ רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Something needed for the Festival, the Rabbis permitted;

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּלָאו צוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב לָא שָׁרוּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: something not needed for the Festival, the Rabbis did not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מוֹעֵד אַאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר קָא רָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to רב ששת than the examples brought by רב פפא and רבינא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the reasons behind two rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything allowed on חול המועד should also be allowed on ערב פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two days restrict work for different reasons, so they cannot be compared.

steps.title: New משנה: moving belongings and bringing utensils from a craftsman
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on חול המועד one may not move belongings from house to house, but may move them into his courtyard. One may not bring utensils home from a craftsman, but if he worries about them, he may move them to another courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not move belongings from house to house, but he may move them to his courtyard. One may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house, but if he is worried about them, he may move them to another courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two rules about moving things during חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving house is a big job that is not needed for the Festival, so it is not allowed. Moving things into one's courtyard is allowed. Bringing finished utensils home from a craftsman is also not allowed. If they might be stolen where they are, he may move them to a safer courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Worried about them, for example that they will be stolen

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not move belongings from house to house,
but he may move them to his courtyard.
One may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house,
if he is worried about them,
he moves them to another courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No moving house and no bringing utensils from a craftsman on חול המועד, with limited exceptions.

steps.title: Didn't the first clause forbid moving altogether?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can allow moving things into a courtyard. Its first clause seemed to forbid moving belongings entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But you said in the first clause that one may not move belongings at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what looks like a contradiction inside the משנה itself. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause sounds like a total ban on moving belongings. The next part of the משנה then allows moving them into a courtyard. The גמרא wants to know how both parts can be true.

phrases.english: GEMARA: But you said in the first clause
that one may not move belongings at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the clauses of the משנה fit together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to move belongings into a courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause seems to forbid all moving, so allowing any moving looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: אביי: the later clause speaks of a house inside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the permitted case is a house that opens onto the courtyard. Moving things from there out into that same courtyard is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The later clause refers to a house that is in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by showing that the two clauses talk about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving from one house to a different house is a real move, and it is forbidden. Moving from a house into its own courtyard is a short, simple transfer, and it is allowed. So the clauses do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (we are now dealing with)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the later clause we have come to a house that is in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְבַיִת שֶׁבֶּחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה both forbids and allows moving belongings, which looks like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covers moving to another house; the permission covers moving from a house into its own courtyard.

steps.title: רבא's test: another משנה allows bringing utensils from a craftsman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports that רבא tested his students with a contradiction. Our משנה forbids bringing utensils from a craftsman, but another משנה allows taking and bringing them, even when they are not needed for the Festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house. רב פפא said: רבא tested us. We learned: One may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house. But a different teaching contradicts this: One may take utensils to the craftsman's house and bring them back, even if they are not needed for the Festival!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the משנה's second rule and sets out a contradiction that רבא used to test his students. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says you may not bring utensils home from a craftsman. Another משנה says you may take them to the craftsman and bring them back, even if they are not for the Festival. Both cannot be true as they stand, so the גמרא must find a way to resolve them.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them (here is a contradicting source)

phrases.english: "And one may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Rava tested us:

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: אֵין מְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאוּמָּן,
phrases.english: We learned: One may not bring utensils from the craftsman's house,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִינְהוּ: מוֹלִיכִין וּמְבִיאִין כֵּלִים מִבֵּית הָאוּמָּן,
phrases.english: and contrast it: One may take utensils to and bring them from the craftsman's house,
phrases.notes: This other teaching is a משנה in פסחים 55b.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד!
phrases.english: even if they are not needed for the Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בָּדֵיק לַן רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first rule of the משנה to its second rule and raises a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one may not bring utensils from a craftsman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה allows taking and bringing utensils from a craftsman even when they are not for the Festival, which directly clashes with our משנה.

steps.title: Two different days: the fourteenth of ניסן versus חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The students answer רבא that the משנה which permits bringing utensils is about ערב פסח, while our משנה which forbids it is about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we answered him: Here, the משנה that permits it is talking about the fourteenth of ניסן. Here, the משנה that forbids it is talking about חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tells us how he and the other students answered רבא's contradiction. Each משנה is talking about a different day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only works if both משניות are about the same day. The students split them apart: the lenient משנה is about ערב פסח, and the strict משנה (ours) is about חול המועד. Each day has its own rules, so a rule for one day does not have to match the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן, which is ערב פסח
The intermediate days of a Festival

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up which side is which. The PERMITTING משנה is about the fourteenth, and OUR משנה, which forbids, is about חול המועד. On this answer, חול המועד is the stricter day for this kind of activity.

phrases.english: And we answered him:
Here, on the fourteenth,
phrases.notes: This is the other משנה, the one that allows bringing utensils. It is talking about the fourteenth of ניסן.

phrases.english: here, on the intermediate days of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁנֵּינַן לֵיהּ: כָּאן בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, כָּאן בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction רבא posed in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is about a different time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to be about the same day, so they appeared to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient משנה is about ערב פסח, and the strict משנה is about חול המועד, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Same day, different situation: trusting the craftsman or not
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: both משניות are about חול המועד. Our משנה forbids it when the owner trusts the craftsman, and the other משנה permits it when he does not trust him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say instead: both משניות are about חול המועד. Here, our משנה forbids it when the owner trusts the craftsman. Here, the other משנה permits it when the owner does not trust the craftsman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to answer רבא. This time both משניות are about the same day, but they are about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of splitting the days, this answer splits the situations. If the owner trusts the craftsman, his utensils are safe there, so there is no loss and no reason to allow moving them. If he does not trust him, the utensils might be lost or stolen, and preventing a loss is a reason the רבנן allow work on חול המועד (Step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (this introduces another possible answer)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to רבא's contradiction. (1) The two משניות are about different days: ערב פסח versus חול המועד. (2) Both are about חול המועד, but in different situations: the owner trusts the craftsman, so he may not bring the utensils, or he does not trust him, so he may.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer fits the reason we already learned for allowing work on חול המועד: preventing a loss. It also matches our own משנה, which allows moving utensils when the owner is worried about them (Step 18).

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
This and that are both about the intermediate days of a Festival.
Here, where he trusts him,
phrases.notes: This is our משנה, which forbids it. The owner trusts the craftsman, so his utensils are safe where they are.

phrases.english: here, where he does not trust him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same contradiction, as an alternative to Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: same time, different circumstances (whether a loss is possible).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both משניות could be about חול המועד, they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing utensils is forbidden when the owner trusts the craftsman and permitted when he does not, because then there is a risk of loss.
